text.p: Today's auction of Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj was suspended, the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange said.
Sergio Berardi, the bourse's superintendent, gave no reasons for the suspension and said no new date was set for the auction.

This was the second time Banerj's sell-off was suspended. Banerj had been due to be auctioned off on December 17, but the sale was postponed due to a court injunction granted to an association of the bank's employees that blocked the sale.
The new date for the auction was set after the Rio de Janeiro state government succeeded in lifting the court order.
Earlier this afternoon a judge ordered the re-evaluation of Banerj's assets based on claims by Banerj employees that they were undervalued.
The court ruling meant the winning bidder would run the risk of having to pay more than the bid price if the court decided that the bank's assets were indeed undervalued.
Banerj and its insurance subsidiary Banerj Seguros were scheduled to be sold for a minimum price of 480 million reais at a closed-envelope privatization auction at 1600 local/1800 GMT.
Bradesco and Banco Itau, the country's two largest private banks, were due to bid for Banerj. ((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro Newsroom, 5521 5074151))
